summary: X's API v2 lets a developer register an app in the Developer Console (console.x.com) and obtain OAuth 2.0 Client ID/Secret (Authorization Code with PKCE) or OAuth 1.0a keys. Access is pay-per-usage with prepaid credits; the docs read do not describe a manual app-review step. Composio's page states Composio-managed OAuth is not available for Twitter, so you must register your own app.
time_to_first_connection: no official figure (docs describe 3 self-serve steps: create developer account, create app, save credentials)
time_to_production: no official figure; the docs read describe no app review or approval wait
effort: Sign in at console.x.com with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, create an app, set app type (Web App/Automated App = confidential; Native/SPA = public), add exact-match callback URLs (max 10), save credentials (shown once), fund the account with credits, and implement the PKCE flow with the scopes you need.

approval.kind: No app review step described in the docs read; developer agreement acceptance and profile completion at signup. Suspension is possible and appealable via the Platform Help Form.
approval.who_reviews: N/A per docs read (X platform team handles suspensions)

steps.title: Create a developer account
steps.detail: Go to console.x.com, sign in with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and complete the profile with basic info on how you will use the API.

steps.title: Add credits / payment
steps.detail: X API v2 is pay-per-usage with purchased credits deducted per request; optionally set a spending limit and auto-recharge (needs a saved payment method).

steps.title: Create an app
steps.detail: Click New App in the console; enter name, description and use case. Keys and tokens are generated.

steps.title: Configure app type, permissions and callback URLs
steps.detail: Choose Web App / Automated App (confidential, gets client secret) or Native / SPA (public, PKCE only). Add callback URLs to the allowlist (max 10, exact match including trailing slashes; https in production, http://127.0.0.1 not localhost for local dev). OAuth 1.0a permission levels are Read, Read+Write, Read+Write+DMs.

steps.title: Save credentials immediately
steps.detail: Credentials are displayed only once; regenerating invalidates the old ones. For OAuth 2.0 you need Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Implement Authorization Code with PKCE
steps.detail: Send users to https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method (S256 or plain). Exchange the code at https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token; codes expire 30 seconds after being received. Include offline.access to get a refresh token (access tokens last two hours by default).

requirements.text: An X account to sign into the Developer Console and acceptance of the Developer Agreement and Policy.
Callback URL(s) registered in the app and matched exactly by redirect_uri.

Scopes documented: tweet.read, tweet.write, tweet.moderate.write, users.read, users.email, follows.read/write, offline.access, space.read, mute.read/write, like.read/write, list.read/write, block.read/write, bookmark.read/write, dm.read/write, media.write, broadcast.read/write.
Funded credit balance for API usage (pay-per-usage).

gotchas.text: Pricing is per-usage and changes: the pricing page (seen 2026-10-20) lists e.g. Post read $0.005, User read $0.010, Post create $0.015, Post create with URL $0.200, Owned Reads $0.001 per resource. The page says prices are subject to change; check the Developer Console.
Pay-per-usage plans are capped at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle; higher volume requires an Enterprise plan (no Enterprise pricing published on that page).
A resource requested more than once in the same 24-hour UTC window is charged once (described as a soft guarantee). A spend cap blocks requests until the next cycle once reached.
Authorization codes expire 30 seconds after receipt; exchange immediately. Without offline.access no refresh token is issued and access tokens last about two hours.
The docs' example authorize URL uses account.follows.read/write, which are not in the scope table (follows.read/write are); verify scope names.

Rate limits are per app (Bearer token) or per user (user tokens), mostly 15-minute or 24-hour windows; e.g. POST /2/tweets is 100/15min per user and 10,000/24hrs per app. Exceeding returns HTTP 429 (code 88). Enterprise has custom limits.
Changing OAuth 1.0a permission level requires users to re-authorize to get tokens with the new scope.
Composio FAQ headings mention errors such as client-not-enrolled / App not linked to project (developer app/project setup issues) and UsageCapExceeded; answers were not visible in the fetched text.

blockers.blocker: Composio-managed OAuth is not available for Twitter
blockers.what_to_do: Register your own X app and supply your Client ID/Secret via a custom auth config in Composio.
Add credits or raise the spending limit in the Developer Console; requests are blocked at the cap until the next cycle.

blockers.blocker: Volume above 3M Post reads per billing cycle
blockers.what_to_do: Contact X via the Enterprise interest form.

agent_can: Build the PKCE authorize URL and handle code exchange and token refresh
Request the needed scopes and handle 429 responses with backoff using x-rate-limit-reset
human_must: Sign into console.x.com and accept the Developer Agreement and Policy
Create the app, set app type and callback URLs
Fund the account and set spend limits

claims.claim: Developer signup is at console.x.com: sign in with X account, accept Developer Agreement, complete profile.
X API v2 uses pay-per-usage pricing with purchased credits and no subscriptions; no free tier described on the pricing page.
Per-resource prices listed on the pricing page as seen 2026-10-20 (see gotchas).
OAuth 2.0 PKCE authorize URL is https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize and token URL is https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token.
Callback URLs: max 10, exact match, use 127.0.0.1 not localhost locally.
Composio-managed OAuth is not available for Twitter.
There is no manual app review gating production use.
Some endpoints or scopes (e.g. DMs, media) may need specific app permissions or may be restricted by plan.
Any signup or approval wait time.

composio.note: Composio's toolkit page states 'Composio-managed OAuth not available' for Twitter and lists OAuth2 as the auth scheme; FAQ headings suggest managed credentials were removed. You must register your own X app and bring your own Client ID/Secret, which means you handle your own branding, scopes, credits and rate-limit/usage quota. Details of the custom auth config were not visible in the fetched text.
